questions.question_text: A fair wheel has $7$ equal sectors labelled $A$ to $G$. Which list records every outcome of one spin exactly once?

options.text: $A,B,C,D,E,F,G$
$A,B,C,D,E,F$
options.why: Leaves out G, so one labelled result is missing from the list.

options.text: $A,B,C,D,E,F,G,G$
options.why: Records G twice even though each possible result should appear once.
Lists sector positions instead of the labels that are recorded after a spin.

questions.solution_text:
Each label is a possible result and is recorded once.
The outcomes are $A,B,C,D,E,F,G$.

questions.question_text: A $5$-sector fair spinner is labelled shell, key, crown, gem and anchor. The list shell, key, crown, anchor is incomplete. Which outcome is missing?

options.text: gem
shell
options.why: Repeats an outcome already recorded instead of finding the omitted label.

options.text: wheel
options.why: Names the random device rather than a possible result shown by its pointer.

options.text: spin
options.why: Names the action in the experiment rather than one of its possible outcomes.

questions.solution_text:
Gem is the only sector label not recorded.
The missing outcome is gem.

questions.question_text: A prize spinner has $4$ equal sectors labelled apple, pear, plum and peach. Which statement is correct?

options.text: All four fruit outcomes are equally likely.
Different fruit labels cannot be equally likely.
options.why: Treats different names as different chances even though their sectors are equal.

options.text: Four possible outcomes must all have different chances.
options.why: Assumes having several outcomes prevents them from sharing the same chance.

questions.solution_text:
Each fruit occupies one equal sector.
All four fruit outcomes are equally likely.

questions.question_text: A fair $6$-sector wheel is labelled $K,K,L,M,N,O$. The letter is recorded. Which statement is correct?

options.text: The letters are not equally likely because K occupies two sectors.
The letters are equally likely because all six sectors are equal.
options.why: Ignores that the two K sectors combine to make K more likely than each other letter.

options.text: The letters are equally likely because every letter is possible.
options.why: Confuses being a possible outcome with having the same chance as every other outcome.

questions.solution_text:
K occupies $2$ equal sectors, while each other letter occupies $1$.
Therefore the recorded letters are not equally likely.

questions.question_text: A wheel is labelled rose, lily and iris. Rose covers half the wheel; lily and iris each cover one quarter. Are the recorded flowers equally likely?

options.text: No, because rose covers more of the wheel.
Yes, because each flower appears as one label.
options.why: Counts label names but ignores the unequal areas assigned to those labels.

options.text: Yes, because only one flower is recorded per spin.
options.why: Confuses recording one result with all possible results having equal chances.

questions.solution_text:
Rose covers $\frac{1}{2}$ of the wheel, while each other flower covers $\frac{1}{4}$.
The flowers are not equally likely.

questions.question_text: A fair spinner is labelled noon, dusk and night. Which description correctly identifies the trial and its outcomes?

options.text: Trial: one spin; outcomes: noon, dusk, night
Trial: noon, dusk, night; outcomes: one spin
options.why: Reverses the experiment action and the possible results of that action.

options.text: Trial: the pointer; outcomes: start, turn, stop
options.why: Names a spinner part and its motion rather than the trial and recorded labels.

questions.solution_text:
The experiment is performed once by spinning once.
The possible recorded results are noon, dusk and night.

questions.question_text: A fair wheel has $7$ different colour labels, including red and indigo. A student lists red twice and leaves out indigo. Which correction produces a complete outcome list?

options.text: Remove the repeated red and add indigo.
Keep both reds and add indigo.
options.why: Adds the missing result but leaves a duplicate, so outcomes are not recorded once each.

options.text: Remove one red and make no other change.
options.why: Removes the duplicate but still leaves the possible indigo result missing.

questions.solution_text:
A complete list records each possible result once.
Remove the repeated red and add the omitted indigo.
